cards.rueckseite:
**Schwannoma:** most common peripheral nerve tumor in adults (NF2, schwannomatosis); eccentric, mobile, flexor surfaces; fascicle of origin usually nonfunctional → **complete resection in ~90%**, pain relief ~90%.
**Neurofibroma:** NF1, **intrafascicular** growth → complete resection harder without deficit; **~10% transform to MPNST** (plexiform).

5–10% of soft-tissue sarcomas; **50% arise from plexiform neurofibromas in NF1**. Warning signs: pain, rapid growth, fixed mass. Worse prognosis: > 5 cm, high grade, NF1, positive margins. 5-year survival **30–50%**. Treatment: **en bloc resection with clear margins** + adjuvant radiation/chemotherapy.

Arises from a nearby joint (classically **superior tibiofibular joint → peroneal nerve**). Disconnect/ligate the **articular branch** (joint connection); complete excision of the intraneural cyst is not needed.

cards.vorderseite: Carpal tunnel syndrome: anatomy, clinic, treatment
cards.rueckseite:
Median nerve under the **transverse carpal ligament**; motor **LOAF** (lumbricals 1–2, opponens, abductor and flexor pollicis brevis). Associations: pregnancy, diabetes, hypothyroidism, acromegaly, RA. **Nocturnal** paresthesias, Phalen, Tinel; palm spared (palmar cutaneous branch). EMG/NCS normal in 15–25%.
Conservative (splint, steroid injection) helps ~50%; otherwise open/endoscopic release. Risk: **recurrent motor branch** injury.

cards.vorderseite: Pronator syndrome vs. carpal tunnel syndrome
cards.rueckseite: Pronator teres syndrome: compression between the two heads of pronator teres; forearm ache, grip weakness. Distinguishing features: **no nocturnal symptoms** and **palmar numbness** (palmar cutaneous branch involved). Usually conservative.
Pure motor branch of the median nerve: **FDP 1–2, FPL, pronator quadratus**. Cannot make an "OK" sign (**pinch sign**), **no sensory loss**. Most resolve in 8–12 weeks; explore if refractory.

- **Froment sign:** thumb IP flexion (FPL substitutes for adductor pollicis)
- **Wartenberg sign:** abducted little finger (weak 3rd palmar interosseous)
- **Claw hand:** digits 4–5 hyperextended at MCP, flexed at IP
- First dorsal interosseous wasting, ulnar sensory loss

Elbow (**cubital tunnel**, between the two heads of FCU) is the most common site. Key: the **dorsal ulnar cutaneous nerve** branches ~6 cm proximal to the wrist → **dorsal hand sensation spared** in Guyon's canal lesions, affected at the elbow.
Surgery at the elbow: decompression, transposition or medial epicondylectomy; divide medial intermuscular septum and arcade of Struthers if transposing.

zeilen: Finger drop, **no wrist drop**, no sensory loss; explore after 8 weeks

cards.rueckseite: At the **suprascapular notch** under the transverse scapular ligament → deep shoulder pain, **supra- and infraspinatus** atrophy (at the spinoglenoid notch: infraspinatus only). Decompression if conservative treatment fails.

**Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (L2–L3)**, purely sensory, ~1 cm medial to the ASIS under the inguinal ligament. Burning lateral thigh. Risk: obesity, diabetes, pregnancy, prone positioning. Conservative success **91%**; decompression or neurectomy if refractory.

cards.vorderseite: Common peroneal nerve vs. tarsal tunnel
cards.rueckseite:
**Peroneal:** at the **fibular head**; foot drop (tibialis anterior, EHL), weak eversion, lateral leg/dorsum sensory loss; inversion spared (vs. L5).
**Tarsal tunnel:** posterior tibial nerve behind/below the **medial malleolus**; burning sole/toes, intrinsic foot weakness.

Rare, women > men; band from a **cervical rib**/C7 transverse process to the first rib. **C8–T1 / lower trunk**: medial forearm numbness, clumsy hand; **Gilliatt–Sumner hand** (thenar > hypothenar atrophy). PT first; decompression (band, first rib resection).

cards.vorderseite: Traumatic nerve injury: timing of repair
cards.rueckseite:
- **Sharp, clean laceration:** primary end-to-end repair within days (72 h)
- **Blunt/contaminated laceration:** tag ends, repair after **~3 weeks** (usually graft)
- **Closed injury:** observe, EMG/NCS after > 3 weeks; explore at **~3 months** if no recovery; intraoperative **NAP**: present → neurolysis, absent → resect and graft (sural)
Early surgery for closed injury only for vascular compromise (hematoma, pseudoaneurysm).

cards.text: Nerve regeneration: recovery order {{c1::autonomic > sensory > motor}}; muscle cannot be reinnervated after about {{c2::18–24 months}}; EMG is reliable only after {{c3::3 weeks}}.
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 643. Regeneration speed ~1 mm/day (1 inch/month).

cards.rueckseite:
**Erb (C5–C6, upper plexus):** downward force on shoulder; "**waiter's tip**" (adducted, internally rotated, elbow extended), hand normal. Better recovery.
**Klumpke (C8–T1, lower plexus):** traction on abducted arm; **claw hand** ± **Horner** (T1). Poor recovery.
Perinatal plexus palsy ~1/1,000 births, 90% spontaneous recovery.

- **Horner syndrome** (T1)
- Weak **serratus anterior** (long thoracic), **rhomboids** (dorsal scapular), **diaphragm** (phrenic)
- **Normal SNAP** in an anesthetic area (dorsal root ganglion intact)
- **Pseudomeningocele** on MRI/myelography
Avulsion → no direct repair possible → **nerve transfers**.

cards.vorderseite: Brachial plexus reconstruction: priorities and donors
cards.rueckseite: Goal: **elbow flexion** first, then shoulder stability/abduction. Best recipient: **musculocutaneous nerve**. Donors: spinal accessory (CN XI), intercostals, phrenic, medial pectoral, cervical plexus, CN XII, fascicles of ulnar/median (Oberlin). Upper plexus: good results > 60%; lower plexus poor.
